The input consists of queries and keys of dimension dk, and values of dimension dv. We compute the dot products of the query with all keys, divide each by √dk, and apply a softmax function to obtain the weights on the values. In practice, we compute the attention function on a set of queries simultaneously, packed together into a matrix Q. The keys and values are also packed together into matrices K and V . We compute the matrix of outputs as: Attention(Q, K, V ) = softmax(QKT √dk )V (1) The two most commonly used attention functions are additive attention [2], and dot-product (multi- plicative) attention. Dot-product attention is identical to our algorithm, except for the scaling factor of 1 √dk . Additive attention computes the compatibility function using a feed-forward network with a single hidden layer. While the two are similar in theoretical complexity, dot-product attention is much faster and more space-efficient in practice, since it can be implemented using highly optimized matrix multiplication code. While for small values of dk the two mechanisms perform similarly, additive attention outperforms dot product attention without scaling for larger values of dk [3]. CÓDIGO
```python
import json
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.default_rng(0)

resultados = {
    "peso_maximo_sin_escalar": {},
    "entropia_bits_sin_escalar": {},
    "peso_maximo_escalado": {},
    "entropia_bits_escalado": {},
}

filas = []
for d_k in [4, 64, 512]:
    q = rng.standard_normal(d_k)
    K = rng.standard_normal((10, d_k))

    puntajes = K @ q

    def softmax(x):
        e = np.exp(x - x.max())
        return e / e.sum()

    p_sin = softmax(puntajes)
    p_esc = softmax(puntajes / np.sqrt(d_k))

    ent_sin = float(-np.sum(p_sin * np.log2(p_sin)))
    ent_esc = float(-np.sum(p_esc * np.log2(p_esc)))

    pm_sin = float(p_sin.max())
    pm_esc = float(p_esc.max())

    resultados["peso_maximo_sin_escalar"][str(d_k)] = pm_sin
    resultados["entropia_bits_sin_escalar"][str(d_k)] = ent_sin
    resultados["peso_maximo_escalado"][str(d_k)] = pm_esc
    resultados["entropia_bits_escalado"][str(d_k)] = ent_esc

    filas.append((d_k, pm_sin, ent_sin, pm_esc, ent_esc))

print(f"{'d_k':>5} | {'peso_max_sin':>13} | {'entropia_sin(bits)':>19} | {'peso_max_esc':>13} | {'entropia_esc(bits)':>19}")
for d_k, pm_sin, ent_sin, pm_esc, ent_esc in filas:
    print(f"{d_k:>5} | {pm_sin:>13.4f} | {ent_sin:>19.4f} | {pm_esc:>13.4f} | {ent_esc:>19.4f}")

with open("resultados.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump(resultados, f, indent=2)

```
